newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded lower on fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings during the shortened holiday week, USDA said.

Retail demand for immediate needs was rather disappointing, but good forward interest was noted for June featuring, especially on closely trimmed items. The rib and loin cuts were under the most pressure as these cuts traded lower throughout the week with the short loin expressing a notable decrease. Round cuts traded at steady levels most of the trading period while chuck cuts traded lower early in the week, but rebounded slightly at weeks end.

Closely trimmed items also traded lower on good demand as these cuts were seen as good values. Fresh beef trimmings traded lower on mostly moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings. Good frozen interest was noted at the end of the trading period. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded mostly lower for immediate needs on moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings. However, a firm undertone was noted for mid June delivery.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.50 to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal .50 to 1.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal steady to 1.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed item's 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Beef trimmings 2.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 3.00 to 5.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.34 at 104.00; 700/850 Dn 1.04 at 103.57; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.71 at 97.34; 700/850 Dn 1.07 at 96.86.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Despite limited slaughter cow receipts in some areas, the lean boneless beef market traded lower this week. This occurred due to continued decreased demand as fast food business remains sluggish.

As a result, trading was slow, and the supplies and offerings increased slightly as the week pro- gressed. The cow cuts, however, traded uneven with the 100% lean items trading lower, despite moderate seasonal demand, for increased inventories. In addition, chuck tenders and knuckles traded at firm price levels on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings.

Utility carcasses steady; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef 2.00-4.00 lower in the Midwest, Texas 5.50 lower; 85% generally 4.50 lower; 75% 1.00-3.00 lower; 65% 2.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, May 29, 1997 was estimated at 77.00 per cwt., down 2.07 from a week ago Friday.
